findings.title: False effective square saturation caused by dropping primitivity

location.claim: Theorem2.6: every unobstructed square n>=8xy is represented; corresponding sufficient square and twice-square lemmas.

assumptions: x=2,y=25 positive coprime; y=1 mod4; Kronecker(2,25)=1; no numerator congruence/reciprocity restriction in Table1.

main.conclusion: No candidate row is primitive, so none belongs to any integral determinant-one matrix.

denominator_lemma.scope: Refutes4xy lemma; not the main8xy bound.

calculation.family: For arbitrary C choose4K>C, m=2t product_{j=0}^{K-1}(4j+3),n=m²,x=1,y=1mod4 strictly between n/(4K+1) and n/(4K). Then every row has b in{3,7,...,4K-1}, each b divides m, and gcd(n-yb,b)=b>1. The orbit varies.

counterevidence: Theorem2.5 square exclusion and Section3 identities survive.
Finite orbit Theorem2.8 independently checked through109120000 and its large twice-square step repaired separately.
No fixed-orbit infinite family of exceptions is claimed.
findings.impact: An advertised effective main conclusion is false; no universal constant replacement Cxy repairs it.

repair.boundary: Retain primitivity indicator and prove a new quantitative primitive-row threshold. No general replacement bound certified.
